incident-bot: [ALERT] Smart-routing pressure detected: economy lane QPS +360% (10m), apac-east P95 latency spiked to ~2300ms, error rate 4.6%. Auto-steer engaged and failing to relieve pressure. Pager: @oncall-alex
oncall-alex: paging in — looking at routing dashboard and KV cache heatmaps :eyes:
sasha-engineer: I can see a small set of keys producing high fanout, KV cache miss ratio jumped. Likely prefix explosion from a new client rollout. Recommend immediate soft throttling on economy tier in apac-east and divert medium requests to dedicated pool if possible.man s
manu-sre: agreed. I'll stage a regional weight update to reduce economy weight in apac-east and enable conservative fallbacks to eu-west. Applying a 30% -> 10% weight change as a canary.

manu-sre: command I ran:```bash
# reduce economy weight in apac-east
rbctl route update --region apac-east --tier economy --weight 0.10 --reason "emergency - lane pressure"
```
deploy-bot: canary applied to apac-east: economy weight now 0.10 for 5m window, will auto-evaluate.
sasha-engineer: after canary: p95 dropped to 950ms, errors down to 1.8% — good signal. Still seeing a tail for a handful of API keys (~5) with very high per-key QPS.
priya-cs: CS note: we've identified 3 paying customers experiencing degraded responses (timeouts ~5-10s). I'm drafting notifications and will open priority support tickets.
ben-platform: quick mitigation option — impose a short token-level RPS cap for anonymous/free tokens and raise soft quotas for enterprise tokens. Can we push quota changes without a restart?
manu-sre: yes, quota adjustments are dynamic. I'll bump enterprise soft-limit +50% for 30m and cap anonymous at 5rps.
manu-sre: commands:
```
kbctl quota set --token-tier anonymous --rps 5 --ttl 1800
kbctl quota inc --token-tier enterprise --rps 50 --ttl 1800
```
oncall-alex: applied. Monitoring. :thumbsup:
priya-cs: notif sent to affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for full resolution.
incident-bot: note created: INC-2026-318888 - "Lane pressure: apac-east economy". Severity: S2.
ben-platform: recommend a follow-up rate-limit rule to reject very high-cardinality prefixes at edge to avoid future prefix explosions. Add to postmortem action items.
onsasha-engineer: agreed — will add a filter to drop requests with >100 unique prefixes/min for the next 24h as a safety net.
oncall-alex: closing page — system stabilized after canary and quotas. Will run postmortem tomorrow with SRE, platform, and CS. Thanks all. :wave:
